history: First successfully colonized extrasolar system, Aurelia III received its initial settlers in 2187 aboard the generation ship New Dawn.
The Aurelian Federation formed in 2298 as colonies across multiple worlds unified under democratic governance.
Today Aurelia rivals Sol itself in population and influence, serving as the anchor of human civilization in this region of space.
description: Aurelia Prime stands as humanity's greatest colonial achievement—eleven billion people across eight worlds and countless stations, all orbiting an ancient yellow sun that has burned steadily for nearly ten billion years. The system's architecture seems designed for habitation: three worlds in the habitable zone, a protective gas giant sweeping debris, and resources distributed conveniently from inner belt to outer ring. Whether this reflects cosmic luck or something more deliberate remains a question philosophers debate in Aurelia Central's halls.

The Aurelian Federation wields influence rivaling Earth's own governments. Its economy drives interstellar commerce; its shipyards produce vessels for dozens of systems; its universities attract students from across known space. Aurelia Central station, with 1.2 million permanent residents, functions as a city in its own right—a crossroads where cultures meet, deals are struck, and humanity's future is shaped in countless daily decisions. Traffic through the system never stops; at any moment, thousands of vessels transit Aurelian space.

Success brings challenges. The Federation struggles with inequality between prosperous Aurelia III and hardscrabble Aurelia II. Immigration pressure strains resources. Rival powers eye Aurelian wealth with envy and occasionally with hostile intent. The dense debris disk that gives The Gauntlet its name provides natural defense but also navigation hazards. Yet for all its problems, Aurelia Prime represents what humanity can build given time and determination—a civilization that spans worlds, anchored by an ancient star that will shine for billions of years to come.
